findings.claim: The hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type flattens the zod discriminated union and makes teamId optional for all scopes. A team-scope call without teamId compiles, fails safeParse at runtime and silently returns empty results; this is also inconsistent with InsightsRoutingService's strict union type.

verifier.reason: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29-34,58, InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions flattens insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema (lines 10-27) and makes teamId optional for all scopes, so a team-scope call without teamId compiles, fails safeParse at lines 62-63 (setting this.options = null), and silently returns NOTHING_CONDITION (1=0) at lines 43,125-128. By contrast, packages/lib/server/service/insightsRouting.ts:29,52 uses the strict z.infer discriminated union InsightsRoutingServiceOptions in its constructor.

findings.claim: The org-scope test assertion depends on the order of ids inside ANY(...) arrays. Those ids come from repository queries (findAllByParentId, MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds) without orderBy, so the SQL-fragment equality is nondeterministic.

verifier.reason: In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:332-343, the org-scope integration test uses toEqual on a Prisma.sql fragment containing ordered ANY(...) arrays for teamIds and userIds. Those arrays are built without sorting in packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:150-169 from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId (packages/lib/server/repository/team.ts:185-198) and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds (packages/lib/server/repository/membership.ts:402-420), neither of which specifies an orderBy clause, making the array order and test equality nondeterministic.
